Hi Maya —

Appreciate the clear notes and the redline. High-level response below and I copied Aditya (AE) and Laura (rev ops) so we can align on operational implications; Neha (legal) has the legal lens.

1) Opt-out window: Redwood would be comfortable with a 60-day written-notice opt-out prior to renewal (we can accept email to the account admin + portal notification as formal notice). That keeps our provisioning planning intact while giving your procurement a predictable window.

2) Non-cancellable initial term: we usually maintain a 12-month non-cancellable initial term for committed discounted pricing. To bridge the gap, we can offer a limited early-exit for a pro-rated termination fee equal to outstanding committed months at the discounted rate, capped at three months' fees.

3) Termination for convenience: we prefer a mutual right with a notice window; if you require unilateral convenience termination with refund mechanics, we need the cap described above to protect capacity commitments.

Neha, can you propose exact contract language (short paragraphs we can insert into the order form)?

Maya — if that high-level approach looks reasonable, we'll produce tracked-change language and send back by Friday. If you prefer a longer notice window (90 days) instead of the termination fee, please let us know and we'll weigh operational tradeoffs.

Folks —

Suggested contract language below (drafted to be concise for insertion into the Order Form):

1) Renewal & Opt-Out: 
"The Initial Term shall be twelve (12) months. Thereafter, this Order Form shall automatically renew for successive twelve (12) month periods unless Customer provides Redwood with written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current Term. Written notice shall be sent to the account administrator on file and to procurement@acmeanalytics.com and may be delivered via email or Redwood's customer portal."

2) Early-Exit and Termination for Convenience:
"Customer may terminate this Order Form for convenience after the first six (6) months of the Initial Term by providing written notice to Redwood. If Customer terminates pursuant to this section prior to the end of the Initial Term, Customer shall pay an early termination fee equal to the lesser of (a) three (3) months' fees at the discounted committed rate, or (b) the pro-rated remaining committed fees calculated by rounding remaining months up to the next full month."

Notes: the combination of a 6-month softening of non-cancellable status + capped fee should address Acme's budget-cycle concern while preserving Redwood's capacity protections.

If the team signs off, I'll produce a tracked change version for their redline review.
